Singapore Police Say Ledger Wallets Sold at Local Retailers Contained Malicious Hardware Implants

Singapore police said on October 28 that some Ledger cryptocurrency hardware wallets purchased from local retailers contained malicious hardware implants capable of stealing users' recovery phrases or private keys. At least two cases have been reported since September 10, resulting in losses of approximately S$3.5 million ($2.7 million). Ledger, a leading French hardware wallet manufacturer, is reviewing the affected cases, while police investigations remain ongoing. — link

Tether Blacklists Dozens of TRON Addresses Holding Approximately $27 Million in USDT

According to TrustSniffer, Tether blacklisted at least 33 addresses on the TRON network on October 28. The figures are based on monitored address balances and do not necessarily represent the exact amount frozen at execution. Tether has not publicly disclosed the reasons for the coordinated blacklisting activity. — link
